stem: How does trauma typically relate to the cause of slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE)?

options.text: It is rarely the actual cause of the condition
It is the primary cause in most cases
It is required for the femoral head to slip
It speeds up recovery from the condition
It prevents slippage of the femoral head

explanation: Trauma is rarely the actual cause of SCFE. The slip usually occurs because of underlying biomechanical and physiological factors rather than a single injury event.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because trauma is often associated with the presentation but is rarely the true underlying cause of SCFE.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because most cases are related to underlying predisposition and mechanical stress, not a single traumatic event.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because SCFE can occur without a specific injury; trauma is not required for the slip to happen.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because trauma is not a treatment and does not improve recovery from SCFE.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because trauma does not prevent slippage; it is not a protective factor in SCFE.

source.hint: Recall if the author views a single injury event as the 'true' cause or a 'perceived' cause.
